title: Like Counter
seoTitle: Design Facebook Likes with Live Counts for Viral Posts
description: Design a like system — recording likes, counting at massive scale for celebrity posts, and pushing live count updates to viewers.
author: Editorial Team

blocks.title: What is a Like Counter?
blocks.text: Every post on a social network shows a like button and a count. The system must record who liked what, show accurate-enough counts, and — for live features — update counts on screen as new likes arrive, even when a celebrity post gets millions of likes in minutes.

items: Users should be able to like and unlike a post (at most one like per user per post).
Users should see the like count on each post, and whether they liked it.
Viewers of a post should see the count update live.

blocks.question: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?

items: Handle bursts of 100k+ likes per second on a single viral post.
Counts may be approximate in real time (lag of a few seconds is fine) but must converge to the exact value.
"Did I like this?" must be accurate for the user (read-your-writes).
Reading counts must be fast (< 50ms) because they appear on every feed item.
**Like**: (postId, userId, createdAt) — the source of truth.
**Like count**: an aggregated counter per post.

blocks.code:
PUT    /posts/:id/like
DELETE /posts/:id/like
GET    /posts/:id/likes/summary -> { count, likedByMe }
SSE    /posts/:id/likes/stream   -> { count } updates

blocks.text: 1) Users should be able to like and unlike

The **Like Service** writes the like edge to a wide-column store keyed by `(postId, userId)` — the primary key makes a like idempotent and enforces one per user. It also emits a `liked`/`unliked` event.
2) Users should see counts and their own like
Counts come from a counter cache (Redis), backed by a durable counts table. "Liked by me" is a point lookup on the likes table, which is accurate immediately after the user's write.

Viewers subscribe over SSE. When a post's count changes, the aggregator publishes the new total to a pub/sub channel for that post; connection servers forward it to subscribed viewers, at most once every second or two.
1) How do we count likes on a viral post?

blocks.title: Increment the post row on every like

approach.text: `UPDATE posts SET likes = likes + 1` per like.

challenges.text: 100k updates per second on one row serialise on its lock and overwhelm the database.
Much faster, but one key still lives on one Redis node — a single hot post can saturate it.

blocks.title: Aggregate events, then shard hot counters

approach.text: Like events go to Kafka, partitioned by postId. Aggregators sum deltas in memory and flush `+N` every second, turning 100k writes into one. For extremely hot posts, also split the counter across shards (`post:123:likes:0..15`) and sum them on read (or cache the sum for a second). A periodic reconciliation job recounts from the likes table so the counter converges to the truth.

challenges.text: Counts lag by about a second and unlike/like flips must be handled as signed deltas.

blocks.text: 2) How do we push live updates to millions of viewers?

Don't send an event per like — that would be 100k messages per second per viewer. Coalesce: emit the latest count per post at most once per second. Fan out hierarchically through pub/sub to connection servers, each of which forwards to its own viewers. For huge audiences, approximate ("1.2M") rather than exact digits.

blocks.title: Pattern: Real-time Updates
blocks.text: Coalescing updates and fanning out to connection servers (not to individual users) is what keeps live counts affordable.

quiz.question: How do you enforce one like per user per post?
What turns 100k likes per second into a manageable write rate?
options: Aggregating deltas in memory and flushing once per second
quiz.explanation: Batching collapses many increments into one.

quiz.question: Why shard a single post's counter?
options: One key on one node can't absorb a celebrity post's write rate
quiz.explanation: Splitting spreads writes across nodes; reads sum the shards.

quiz.question: How should live counts be pushed to viewers?
options: Coalesced updates at most once per second
quiz.explanation: Viewers only need the latest number.
